clue.text: Typical weight gain between 500 and 1000 years ago, before the present era

parts.note: the medieval period, roughly 500 to 1500 AD, is known as the Middle Ages
pre- is the prefix meaning before
AD, Anno Domini, labels years of the present era

explanation.surface: A dating puzzle about some historical period before our era, dressed up as a remark about weight.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like history, but the dates are just a loose way of describing the medieval period; the rest gives PRE and AD.
explanation.definitionFit: The thickening waistline that commonly arrives in one's forties or fifties is the classic weight gain of mid-life.

clue.text: Fool's stolen record made by police

parts.note: a mug is a gullible fool; with the possessive it gives MUGS
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A fool's stolen item becomes evidence in a police file.
explanation.definitionFit: Police photograph an arrested suspect's face as an official record of the arrest.

clue.text: Play with a tot first

indicators.note: first places the tot ahead of the a in the answer

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick drink before a theatre performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of theatre, which is a work of drama.

clue.text: Get a move on making appearance with instrument

parts.note: looks means one's appearance
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: Someone is told to hurry up while showing up with a musical instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urging someone to be quick and alert is a way of telling them to hurry.

clue.text: Vessel made slow passage, having dropped line

indicators.note: having dropped tells us a letter is lost from the musical word

parts.note: largo is a musical term for a slow movement or passage

explanation.surface: A ship made slow progress after losing a mooring rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passage' suggests a voyage, fitting the vessel, but it is a passage of music, played largo.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Jason and the Argonauts sailed in this ship, so it is a famous vessel.

clue.text: A German saint, a German who strove for world peace

parts.note: ein is German for a, so a German word for a
again ein, the German for a

explanation.surface: A description of a German-born saintly figure who campaigned for peace.
explanation.walkthrough: Each 'a German' is the German word for 'a', not a person; the definition is the descriptive tail.
explanation.definitionFit: The physicist was a lifelong pacifist who campaigned against nuclear weapons after the war.

clue.text: In America, Dad takes a large slice of Indian bread

indicators.note: a large slice means most of the bread is kept and its tail is cut away

parts.note: a poppadom is a thin crisp Indian bread

explanation.surface: A father in the United States helps himself to a big piece of Indian bread.
explanation.walkthrough: Only most of the bread is used: cut DOM from the end of POPPADOM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an American informal word for father, like pop or pa.

clue.text: Journalist circling library aimlessly — he's arrived before time

indicators.note: circling means the journalist's letters go round the others

parts.note: ED, short for editor, is the crossword journalist

indicators.note: aimlessly means the letters of library wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A reporter wanders around a library and turns up early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Journalist' is the crossword's usual editor; 'aimlessly' is the anagram signal and 'circling' the container, so the man in the library is not the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who turns up ahead of schedule is described by the proverbial worm-catching bird.

clue.text: Systematic search? It's somewhat chaotic, granted

indicators.note: somewhat chaotic says the letters of granted are put into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone concedes that the situation is fairly disorderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat chaotic' rearranges GRANTED.
explanation.definitionFit: A police operation that sweeps an area thoroughly for suspects is a systematic search.

clue.text: Cricket club employing attractive medium

parts.note: glam, short for glamorous, means attractive
an organ is a medium of communication, such as a newspaper

explanation.surface: A sports club takes on a good-looking psychic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a clairvoyant, but it is a medium of communication, an organ. GLAMORGAN is a Welsh county side in English first-class cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: This Welsh county fields one of the first-class county cricket teams.

clue.text: Put down casually, a jacket

parts.note: to park something is informally to set it down somewhere

explanation.surface: A jacket is dumped carelessly somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a hooded windproof jacket, originally an Inuit garment.

clue.text: Husky sounding like a large animal

indicators.note: sounding like says the answer is spoken like the animal word

parts.note: a horse is a large animal

explanation.surface: A sled dog that resembles a big beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the dog but is the adjective for a rough voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A husky voice is rough and croaky, just like one strained by a cold.

clue.text: Desperate to end, say "Don't be so hasty!"

indicators.note: desperate letters are in turmoil, so to end say is rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone eager to finish is told to slow down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' rearranges TO END SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is a common British appeal for someone to calm down and slow up.

clue.text: Topping coat sailor has on

indicators.note: has on places the sailor in front of the coat in the across answer

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh

explanation.surface: A sailor wears a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' looks like an adjective meaning excellent, but it is a road surface laid on top.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the surfacing material laid on roads and runways, a top layer.

clue.text: Dog roses perhaps improved when deadheaded

parts.note: roses are examples of reds, red flowers

indicators.note: deadheading removes a flower's head, so the first letter is cut off

parts.note: better means improved

explanation.surface: Roses do better after the dead blooms are snipped off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when deadheaded' takes the first letter from BETTER, leaving ETTER. It is a garden term, apt with roses.
explanation.definitionFit: An Irish setter, the red-coated gundog, is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Literal interpretation of road race

parts.note: the M1 is a British motorway, read as M and I
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: Someone takes a road race at face value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literal' is a printer's term for a typing error, not an adjective. The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with the 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: In printing jargon a literal is a typographical error in the text.

clue.text: Writing material to be read by pre-eminent people, in part

indicators.note: in places the chief people inside the abbreviation for part

parts.note: arch, as in archbishop, means chief or pre-eminent
men means people

explanation.surface: Some text is to be read out by important figures, in part.
explanation.walkthrough: PT, an abbreviation, holds ARCH and MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Treated animal skin was the traditional surface for writing on before paper.

clue.text: Very many play quaveringly before number one turns up

parts.note: to trill is to play a rapidly wavering note

indicators.note: turns up in a down answer means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A musician plays a warbling note before the leading performer appears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses NO and I into ION.
explanation.definitionFit: A million million is an enormous figure, used loosely for a huge number.

clue.text: Alter ego accompanying Mun go in capital grassland

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the evil alter ego of Dr Jekyll
Mungo Park was a Scottish explorer of Africa, printed broken across a line

explanation.surface: A split personality goes along with an explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: HYDE PARK is a large park in central London, the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a large royal park of open grass in central London.

clue.text: Superior part of drum kit

definitions.meaning: snobbish and haughty, putting on airs
a pair of cymbals worked by a foot pedal in a drum set

explanation.definitionFit: The word means snooty and also names the pedal-operated cymbals beside the snare drum.

clue.text: Dealer rejected Russian paintings

indicators.note: rejected means the pieces are sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: red was a common label for a Soviet Russian communist
paintings are art

explanation.surface: A dealer turns down some paintings from Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian' as red is a Cold War convention; the single 'rejected' turns the whole two-word phrase round, not just one piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is one who buys and sells goods, a dealer.

clue.text: Resurrection of Frenchman upset the legal profession

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: law is the legal profession

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's revival annoys lawyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses LAW to WAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revival or restoration to life, as of a church or a lease, is a renewal.

clue.text: Propagandist leaves without returning — left to fade away

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leaving word goes round the rest

parts.note: goes means leaves

indicators.note: returning means those pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to ebb is to fade away

explanation.surface: A propaganda chief departs without coming back, abandoned to decline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the pair round and 'without', in its old sense of outside, wraps the leaving word around them. Goebbels was Hitler's propaganda minister.
explanation.definitionFit: He ran the Nazi propaganda ministry, the most notorious propagandist of the Third Reich.

clue.text: Feel blue and down

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means to be sad; as one word it means beneath.

clue.text: Select part of Asia once

definitions.meaning: an old name for Korea under Japanese rule

explanation.definitionFit: The word means picked out, and was also the historic name used for Korea.

clue.text: The strength of exotic wines

indicators.note: exotic suggests something foreign and unusual, so wines is rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark on the potency of unusual wines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' rearranges WINES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinew means muscular power, as in the sinews of war.

clue.text: Chase Henry and the rest, going on ahead

indicators.note: going on ahead puts the and-the-rest piece before the other

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means and the rest
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone pursues Henry and his followers, who have gone on in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chase' is not pursue but the metalworker's verb, to engrave.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase metal is to engrave decoration into it, and so is to etch.

clue.text: Letter of the alphabet at which you can stop

definitions.meaning: the NATO phonetic code word for H
a place to stay the night

explanation.definitionFit: It is the radio code word for H and also an inn where travellers stay.

clue.text: Having been informed, we think no differently

indicators.note: differently means the letters of we think no are put in another order

explanation.surface: Being well informed, we hold another view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges WE THINK NO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means aware of inside information, as someone briefed.

clue.text: Make a concession — charge nothing for additional item

definitions.meaning: admit defeat, give up the fight
read literally, giving a free towel as an extra

explanation.definitionFit: The boxing idiom means to concede defeat; literally a seller gives a towel free as a bonus.
